COMPANY OVERVIEW

The built world generates more data than almost any other industry. Almost none of it is being used. Rentana is changing that, building the AI copilot for real estate that distills billions of real-world signals into revenue intelligence, so operators can optimize every lever across their portfolio and actually talk to their data.



Our founding team has built four multi-billion dollar software companies and two proptech exits, including Dynasty (sold to AppFolio) and Urbandoor (sold to Airbnb). Our founding engineers include the first engineer at Airtable and the engineer who led the largest code migration in Stripe's history.



Customers love Rentana: we are the top-rated revenue management platform on Revyse, with NMHC Top 50 real estate owners and operators on the platform within 1 year of public launch.




ROLE

We're building something special at Rentana, and we need someone exceptional to help us scale it. This role sits in the Office of the CEO, which means you'll have direct visibility into the most important decisions in the business and a real hand in shaping how we grow.



The work is intentionally broad. Some weeks that means finding and closing exceptional candidates. Other weeks it means designing the process that didn't exist yet, building the financial model that clarifies a big decision, or writing the playbook that turns a one-time win into a repeatable system. If you're hyper-organized, fired up by high ownership, and get genuine satisfaction from bringing structure to a fast-moving company, this role was built for you.



This role will be in person in NYC with the Office of the CEO.




KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

 - Recruiting. You'll support managing hiring end-to-end: sourcing, pipeline management, candidate experience, and closing. We're building a world-class team and you'll be central to that.

 - Finance & Billing. Translate product data into billing in Quickbooks, manage ARR tracking, and support our financial model. You'll be the person who keeps the numbers clean and current.

 - Customer Success Ops. Use Hex, SQL, and internal dashboards to build polished, executive-ready presentations that tell the story of client ROI and performance. You'll also build the process that makes this repeatable at scale.

 - Business Operations. You'll spot where things are starting to strain before they break, then build the systems and processes that fix them. Documentation, playbooks, structure — you'll be the one who creates it.

 - Strategy. You'll work directly with the founding team on questions that don't have obvious answers yet: competitive positioning, market strategy, go-to-market sequencing. Real seat at the table.

 - Special Projects. If it matters to the business and no one owns it yet, it probably lands here. You’re excited by that.




NICE TO HAVE

 - 2–6 years of experience in consulting, finance, investing, ops, or a generalist role at a startup

 - Strong written and verbal communication, you can synthesize fast and write clearly

 - Financial modeling and Deck building skills

 - Demonstrated ability to operate independently and figure things out, passion for AI tools

 - Hyper organized and enjoy creating systems and process




WHAT WE OFFER

 - The opportunity to be part of a pioneering team in a high-growth industry, shaping the future of AI in real estate.

 - Direct collaboration with the startup’s top leadership, offering a unique insight into business management and strategic decision-making.

 - A competitive salary with equity options.

 - Comprehensive benefits package including health, dental, and vision insurance.

 - A dynamic, innovative, and supportive work environment.

ABOUT ALEPH

Aleph is an AI-native platform for Financial Planning & Analysis (FP&A), an established software category with a multi-billion market but no clear winner. We’re trying to solve a problem many finance teams are super familiar with: data scattered across a million systems, endless spreadsheets and way too much time spent getting numbers to line up instead of actually using them to make decisions.

Aleph was founded by Albert Gozzi and Santiago Perez De Rosso, two technical founders with backgrounds from Stanford and MIT and experience working at top-tier companies such as Google, Microsoft and Bain & Company. We’re backed by top VCs (Khosla Ventures, Bain Capital Ventures, YC, Picus Capital), and work with customers like Webflow, Notion, Zapier, Y Combinator and many others.

We are hiring remotely across the Americas (United States, Canada, LATAM).




🔍 WHAT WE’RE LOOKING FOR

Aleph is looking for a Strategic Business Development Lead to run demos and proofs of concept with FP&A leaders as they evaluate Aleph. Think of this as a sales engineer role built around FP&A. Instead of teaching engineering concepts to technical buyers, you're teaching AI and automation concepts to finance leaders. You'll act as the subject matter expert on both FP&A best practices and the product, owning technical evaluations from first demo through decision.


This role sits at the intersection of finance expertise and sales execution. You'll be deep in the product and in prospects' financial workflows, and the job is ultimately about winning technical evaluations and earning trust fast.




👷 WHAT YOU’LL BE DOING

 - Showcase Aleph’s AI-native approach in action: Lead product demos and POCs that highlight how Aleph automates spreadsheet-heavy FP&A workflows using AI. You’ll own the technical proof points (demos, POCs and deep dive Q&A) and demonstrate how Aleph replaces manual work without forcing teams to abandon their spreadsheets

 - Run high-conviction, short-cycle trials: Design and lead fast-paced trials that deliver clear value in days, not months. You’ll work directly with stakeholders to configure solutions, answer edge-case questions, and accelerate the path to yes

 - Engage senior finance leaders on AI and outcomes: Speak credibly with CFOs and VPs about where AI fits in finance. You’ll answer hard finance questions, translate technical features into business value, and position Aleph as a strategic partner, not just a tool

 - Close the loop between buyer needs and product direction: Work closely with GTM, Product, and Engineering teams to refine Aleph’s positioning and roadmap -- especially around AI-first workflows and features. You’ll bring back real-world insights that help us sell smarter and build better




📝 WHAT YOU BRING

 - 5+ years in finance, PE, FP&A, or consulting -- you hold your own with a CFO

 - Fast and sharp in a spreadsheet; confident building and defending a model

 - Can translate fluently between finance and product speak

 - Able to thrive in ambiguity and move fast on your own

 - Curious about AI and can make the case for it to a skeptic

 - Remote-ready and self-directed on a distributed team

 - Nice-to-have:
   
   - Startup experience
   
   - Hands-on with SQL/BI tools
   
   - Previous sales engineering or similar experience

You'll go deep on a small set of strategic technology partners that matter most to how enterprises build with data and AI, and turn each one into a durable, multi-year relationship. As SpaceXSI's single owner for each partner, you'll own the executive relationship, joint strategy, product and integration alignment, and the co-sell and co-marketing motion that drives customer adoption and pipeline. This role is built for depth, not breadth, and sits at the center of how we work with Product, Engineering, Sales, and Marketing to make each partnership show up in real customer outcomes.

PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:

HI! WE ARE CHAPTERS.

Chapters is a multi-product tech company that spots big consumer problems and builds products that become part of everyday life for millions. Our goal is to build one of the world’s leading consumer tech companies, and the next generation of leaders who’ll build global businesses.

We are looking for a Business Associate to join our team and help turn data into strategic decisions that drive growth and margin directly alongside our founders and leadership team

How Will You Make an Impact?

 - Work directly with founders and top management, translating data into strategic decisions that move the P&L, not just slide decks

 - Own the full analytics lifecycle — from raw data to business recommendation — using internal metrics and external benchmarks to identify growth levers and margin opportunities

 - Independently identify and launch initiatives that improve efficiency, unit economics, and profitability

 - Conduct systematic competitive and market analysis to uncover new growth and monetization opportunities

 - Build business cases and analytical frameworks that directly shape strategic decisions — and take ownership of seeing them through

 - Drive strategic initiatives end-to-end, measuring progress against concrete business and margin outcomes

What Makes You a Perfect Fit?

 - 3-5 years of experience in strategic consulting, investment banking, Private Equity, Venture Capital, or corporate finance

 - Strong analytical skills: experience conducting market research, competitive analysis, financial modeling, and preparing data-driven recommendations

 - Hands-on experience using AI tools for research, workflow automation, and improving the efficiency of analytical work

 - Genuine interest in seeing the big picture — working across multiple cross-functional contexts and understanding how every part of the business operates and connects

 - High ownership, high standards, and a track record of delivering high-quality results — holding yourself and others to that same bar

Even Better If You Have:

 - Experience independently managing strategic projects end-to-end — from problem definition to implementation (full ownership)

 - Experience in Investor Relations, preparing investor materials, or supporting investment transactions (M&A, fundraising)

 - Experience with SQL, Python, or BI tools

What Will You Enjoy Most About Being at Chapters?

 - Culture of Curiosity: no playbook? Good. We dig deeper until we find what actually moves the business.

 - Growth through Impact: ready for more? Take it. The value you bring defines how far you go, from your first role to launching and leading a new product.

 - Trust and Ownership: the freedom to act and make decisions, with full ownership of the outcome.

 - Expert Community: level up faster, working with global partners and people who raise the bar.

 - Sport & Clubs: sport sections and professional clubs for sharing expertise, so there’s always a place to recharge and grow.

 - Space for Ambition: offices in Kyiv, Lviv and Warsaw, built to keep your energy and focus high.

 - Support During the War: we provide conditions for stable work and contribute to Ukraine’s recovery together.

Ready for Your Next Chapter?

If ambitious goals spark your curiosity, you’ll fit right in. Bring your drive, and let’s see how far it takes you.

Pace is the AI operations partner for the world's leading insurers. We deploy AI agents, backed by our expert insurance operations review, to take on complex insurance workflows end to end. Financial services spend nearly $400B a year on outsourced operations. We’re building the layer that replaces it, working alongside the largest insurers in the world.

 


ROLE

We’re looking for a Strategic Accounts Manager to embed deep P&C industry expertise directly within PACE’s largest client engagements. This role partners closely with client operations leaders, PACE’s Forward Deployed Engineers, and Human Quality Teams to translate operational objectives into scaled, production-grade agentic operations.

 

The Strategic Accounts Manager serves as the connective tissue between strategy and execution – accelerating adoption, anticipating operational and regulatory risk, and ensuring seamless transitions from pilot to enterprise scale. Success in this role is defined by measurable client outcomes, disciplined risk management, and the expansion of agentic capabilities across the client’s operating model.

 


RESPONSIBILITIES

 1. Own Strategic Client Outcomes for Agentic Operations Serve as the primary executive partner to PACE’s largest P&C clients, accountable for translating client operational goals (cost, speed, quality, growth) into scaled, production-grade agentic operating models. Ensure outcomes are measured in business KPIs.

 2. Translate P&C Domain Expertise into Agentic Design Bring deep P&C operational knowledge (underwriting, policy admin, claims, distribution) directly into solution design by guiding Forward Deployed Engineers and Human Quality Teams on how workflows should be sequenced to maximize impact while maintaining regulatory and risk discipline.

 3. Orchestrate Cross-Functional Delivery at Scale Act as the connective tissue between client operations leaders, PACE’s Forward Deployed Engineers, and Human Quality Teams by ensuring rapid alignment, clear decision rights, and disciplined execution as agentic solutions move from pilot to scaled production across the enterprise.

 4. Anticipate and Mitigate Operational, Regulatory, and Adoption Risk Proactively identify risks associated with agentic transitions—model drift, exception handling gaps, regulatory exposure, or quality degradation—and partner with clients and internal teams to design controls, escalation paths, and human-in-the-loop strategies before significant issues arise.

 5. Shape Long-Term Account Strategy and Expansion Define the multi-year roadmap for each strategic account, identifying where agentic capabilities can expand beyond initial use cases into adjacent operations. Serve as the voice of the client inside PACE, influencing product evolution, talent strategy, and investment priorities to deepen partnership value over time.

 


OUR TEAM

We’re building a small, talent-dense team with a few defining traits:

 

 1. Integrity: We care about working with good people who want to create a massive impact in the world. Our team aims to do the best work of their careers, knowing that it will take time and focus to build something enduring.

 2. Ambition: We’re building a category-defining company: an AI-native operations layer that brings outsourced work back in-house for insurers – and eventually other service-heavy industries. We’re looking for people who want real ownership, an exceptional bar, and the chance to build something generational.

 


COMPENSATION & BENEFITS

 - Competitive base salary + meaningful early-stage equity

 - Full medical, dental, and vision coverage

 - Unlimited PTO

 

At Pace, we're building a talent-dense team where teammates grow into leaders. This might mean growing into a world-class IC, owning a line of business, or leading teams. Whichever your path, we want to support you to grow at Pace and beyond for the long-term.

The ideal candidate is not a “hard closer.”

They are a trusted advisor, a confident communicator, and someone who can create genuine “aha moments” during the conversation.

If you’ve ever thought:

   …this may be exactly the opportunity you’ve been looking for.

A dedicated planning team handles implementation after the client enrolls.

This role is ideal for professionals who:

WHY TOP PERFORMERS LOVE THIS OPPORTUNITY:

 - No cold calling or prospecting

 - Sophisticated financial conversations with affluent clients

 - High-ticket consultative sales environment

 - Extensive coaching and ongoing development

 - High-performance culture without toxic sales pressure

 - Opportunity to sell a service that genuinely changes lives


MAJOR ROLES & RESPONSIBILITIES:

 - Conduct inbound Zoom consultations with qualified prospects.

 - Use the client’s diagnostic framework to assess retirement planning concerns and tax exposure risks.

 - Educate prospects on retirement tax mitigation and Roth conversion planning concepts.

 - Create meaningful “epiphany moments” that help prospects

About the job

Company Overview
Our client is an early-stage, fast-growing beauty brand redefining the nail care category with high-performance skincare for nails. Founded by seasoned beauty and consumer leaders, including the former CEO of a global beauty brand and the founder of a category-defining DTC consumer brand, the company sells across its own DTC e-commerce channel, national retail partners in the US, TikTok Shop, and Amazon. It is now scaling an omnichannel acquisition model that connects direct-to-consumer digital channels with its national retail footprint.

About the Role
Maybe you’ve been running paid media on autopilot and miss the rigor of real experimentation. Or maybe you’ve been testing creative inside a big agency and want to see your results move a brand’s numbers directly. In this role you won’t follow a generic media buying playbook. You’ll approach paid acquisition like a testing engineer: design the experiments, read the data, scale what works, and cut what doesn’t.

What You Will Do
This is a hands-on role for a rigorous, data-obsessed media buyer who lives inside ad accounts and spreadsheets. Every platform behaves differently. The expectation stays the same: acquire customers efficiently and prove it with data.
You will build, manage, and optimize paid acquisition campaigns across Meta, TikTok, Google/YouTube, and retail ad networks such as Target Roundel and Amazon Ads. You will run structured creative testing frameworks across hooks, formats (static vs. motion), landing pages, and value propositions to systematically find winning ad concepts. To drive in-store sales, you will design and monitor geo-targeted campaigns around key retail stores to lift foot traffic and register velocity. You will manage daily budget pacing, ROAS thresholds, blended MER, and first-order CAC in real-time tracking spreadsheets. Each week, you will give the Senior Graphic Designer and Content & Community Manager a data readout on creative fatigue, winning visual elements, and next-sprint asset requests. You will also use AI analysis tools and custom scripts to evaluate attribution models, track ad trends, and speed up weekly reporting.

Why Join
You’ll join a fast-growing brand at an early stage, backed by founders with deep beauty and consumer experience. You’ll have real ownership of the paid acquisition engine across DTC, marketplaces, and national retail, and you’ll work closely with a small in-house growth team where your tests directly shape the business. The role is fully remote and works with a US-based team.

Who You Are

 - Performance Media Buying Track Record: 3–5+ years directly deploying and managing paid media budgets for consumer or e-commerce brands on Meta, TikTok, and Google.

 - Testing Discipline: Demonstrated ability to manage structured creative testing frameworks and scale winning ad creative without degrading efficiency.

 - Spreadsheet & Analytical Fluency: High comfort with CAC/LTV calculations, blended MER modeling, and third-party attribution platforms (Triple Whale, Northbeam, or GA4).

 - Execution Autonomy: Independent problem-solver who monitors campaign efficiency proactively and makes swift optimization calls.

 - Language & Alignment: Fluent English communication; full schedule alignment with US Eastern hours.

Nice to Have

 - Familiarity with marketplace advertising (Amazon Ads) or retail media networks (Target Roundel)

 - Experience in beauty, personal care, or CPG, especially replenishable products

 - Experience running geo-targeted campaigns to drive retail foot traffic

 - Comfort writing scripts or using AI tools to automate reporting and analysis

ABOUT ARCA

Arca is a wealth management firm built from the ground up with AI. Most people get financial advice that's reactive: an annual check-in, a plan that's a document instead of a living thing, a relationship where you're one of three hundred clients your advisor is trying to remember. We think that's backwards. The kind of service that used to require a team of specialists behind you, the kind that makes you feel like the only person in the room, should be available to far more than the ultra-wealthy.



So we're building it. We're not SaaS — we are the wealth management business, rebuilding it from the inside with AI. Our platform is an Iron Man suit for advisors: it takes over the low-leverage work so they can focus on what actually requires a human, showing up with empathy, context, and judgment. Underneath, it keeps a living understanding of each client. It remembers the thing you mentioned once, six months ago. It notices when your life changes — a new job, a new kid, a market shift — and adjusts before you think to ask. You won't see the technology. You'll just notice your advisor seems to know you better than any financial professional ever has.



That's the product we're growing: client by client, on the strength of the experience itself. We started by acquiring firms managing over $1B in client assets, which gave us real advisors, real clients, and real financial outcomes to build against from day one. But acquisition was the starting line. The bet is that an advisor backed by this platform delivers something good enough that clients come to us on their own.



It's a $20T market, and we think it's ready to be rebuilt.

— Rron, CEO




THE RECEIPTS

 - Stage: Series A, $64M raised

 - Backed by: General Catalyst, Index Ventures, Venrock

 - Board & Advisors: Former CEO of Vanguard, Former CFO of Schwab, Founder of Altruist, Morgan Housel (author of The Psychology of Money)




THE TEAM

We’re small on purpose and engineering heavy: about 80% of the team is technical. We’re based in NYC and hail from high growth startups like Stripe, Ramp, Rippling, Plaid, Doordash, & Glean.

We’re fully in-office in Flatiron, five days a week—lunch together, coffee breaks, basketball games, happy hours.

As a Member of Corporate Development focused on M&A, you're a key part of Arca's growth engine. We grow by acquiring RIAs — typically ~$500M-to-$2B+ AUM firms led by a founder thinking carefully about their next chapter — and putting our platform underneath them. Your job is to find those firms, build real relationships with the people who run them, and carry deals from the first coffee to close. For a founder deciding what happens to the firm they spent a career building, you're the person they come to trust to get them there.

This is a high-ownership seat with a direct line to the Head of M&A and senior leadership. You own relationships, you shape the pipeline, and you see your work in every firm we bring on. Acquisition is how the whole company grows, so the deals you close set the pace for everything else.




WHAT YOU'LL OWN

ABOUT ORNN

Ornn is building the financial infrastructure for AI compute. Our price indices are live on Bloomberg Terminal. We structure and trade compute hedging instruments. And we're now building a platform that brings exchange-grade mechanics like order management, matching, scheduling, and settlement to how compute capacity gets reserved and allocated. We're a lean team in New York, backed by leading venture and strategic investors.



ABOUT THE ROLE

Working directly with Ornn's counsel, you would review and mark up MSAs, order forms and service level agreements, track what is outstanding, and keep contracts moving. Most of it is careful, methodical work on standard paper.

This is a role for someone with real legal training who would rather see how commercial contracts work at a company building a new market than review the hundredth version of the same document at a firm.



WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Review and redline customer MSAs, order forms and service level agreements against our standard positions.

 - Prepare first drafts, and turn counsel's comments into clean language.

 - Track every contract in flight: which version is current, whose turn it is, and how long it has been sitting.

 - Support supplier paperwork: NDAs, diligence documents and onboarding.

 - Take contract questions off the go-to-market team so they can sell.




Requirements

 - A JD, a paralegal certificate, or late-stage enrollment in a law program. This role needs real legal training, not an adjacent degree.

 - Experience reviewing commercial contracts, or clear evidence you can pick it up quickly.

 - Precise and methodical. In this job the detail is the work.

 - Able to run a queue and chase people without being asked twice.

 - Discreet with confidential commercial terms.

 - Based in New York and able to work in person at our office.


Nice-to-Haves

 - Experience with technology, services or infrastructure contracts, particularly MSAs and service level agreements.

 - Time in an in-house legal team at a startup rather than only at a firm.

 - Interest in commercial or commodity markets, or in how compute is becoming an asset class.

 - Familiarity with DocuSign and contract management tools.



WHY THIS ROLE MATTERS

Ornn sells capacity it does not own, under contracts that promise availability and delivery dates. When our customer paper and our supplier paper do not line up, we carry the difference. Catching that at review is far cheaper than discovering it at a service credit. This role is how the paper keeps up with the deal flow, and how the rest of the team stops doing legal work on the side.



COMPENSATION AND BENEFITS

Benefits include competitive salary, meaningful equity, health coverage, free meals, and additional benefits. This is an early role with significant impact and equity upside.



EQUAL OPPORTUNITY STATEMENT

Ornn is committed to building a diverse team. We evaluate candidates based on their ability to do the work, not on pedigree or background. We encourage applications from people of all backgrounds and experiences.

We’re proud of what we’ve accomplished in such a short time and look forward to sharing this journey with you. Join us as we continue to scale, diversify our portfolio, and grow with the evolving community of gamers. 




ABOUT YOUR TEAM

Our Customer Support operation is scaling and becoming more automated. As our first dedicated Customer Support Data Analytics Engineer, you’ll sit in Operations and work hand in hand with the Customer Support team, the Head of Operations, Product, Engineering, Payments and Risk. You’ll explain why customers contact us, measure what self-service and automation actually resolve, and help the team decide what to fix first based on evidence.

You’ll work with Databricks (SQL), Kustomer, QuickSight, Mixpanel, Jira and Slack, on top of an internal data layer with Claude integrated. Current focus: AI and automation in support, and building and optimising our support metric stack.




RESPONSIBILITIES

 - Reusable data models: Build and maintain dbt models on Databricks across bronze, silver and gold layers, with tests, column documentation and incremental logic, so the next person can build on them.

 - Data mapping and feasibility: Know what data we have, what is missing and how it connects. Join sources that were never designed to be joined, audit contact tagging so reporting stays reliable, and judge early whether a requested metric is buildable. If it isn’t, say exactly which data is missing and what it would take to get it.

 - Metric design: Turn vague requests from the Customer Support team into exact metric definitions, such as repeat contact, automated deflection rate and cost per contact, and prove each one against raw data before it ships.

 - Dashboards and reporting: Build dashboards end to end in QuickSight and Omni (datasets, calculated fields, filters). Deliver weekly support performance packs with actionable insights and thresholds for ops managers and leadership.

 - Daily operations pulse: Monitor volumes, backlog, SLAs and CSAT to flag spikes early. Investigate “this number looks wrong” cases by tracing a visual back through the model to the source table.

 - Contact-driver and feedback analysis: Identify why customers contact us by product, spot growing issues, and analyse QA and customer feedback to surface coaching themes and process gaps.

 - Automation and self-service: Measure how well AI, bots and help content resolve issues, including repeat contacts and CSAT.

 - Root-cause partnership: Partner with Product, Payments and Risk to quantify the impact of issues and track fixes.

 - Planning input: Help forecast contact volume and capacity needs.




REQUIREMENTS

 - 3+ years of experience as a Data Analytics Engineer in Customer Support, contact-centre or CX environments.

 - Strong SQL, dbt and hands-on experience with BI and reporting tools (we use QuickSight; Power BI, Looker or similar is fine).

 - Solid knowledge of customer support metrics and contact-driver analysis: CSAT, FCR, handling time, repeat contact, deflection.

 - Ability to turn insights into operational changes with non-technical stakeholders.

 - Curiosity about why customers get in touch and what would stop the issue from happening again. You care more about changing outcomes than producing dashboards.

 - Good written and spoken English (proficiency preferred).


NICE TO HAVE

 - Python or text analytics on ticket data.

 - Experience with a support CRM’s data

About Ornn

Ornn is building the financial infrastructure for AI compute. Our price indices are live on Bloomberg Terminal. We structure and trade compute hedging instruments. And we're now building a platform that brings exchange-grade mechanics like order management, matching, scheduling, and settlement to how compute capacity gets reserved and allocated. We're a lean team in New York, backed by leading venture and strategic investors.

About the Role

Ornn Compute bundles compute reservations from non-investment grade tenants into diversified baskets that a neocloud can underwrite as a single, more creditworthy counterparty. This role will control the structuring of those baskets: how the tranching works, how credit enhancement layers in, how the pool performs under stress, and how it all gets presented to rating agencies and institutional buyers.

You will design the credit structures that sit at the core of Ornn's value proposition, working directly with the founders to define how tenant pools are composed, how risk is allocated across tranches, and how the resulting instruments are rated and distributed. You will be the person in the room with credit ratings agencies, walking them through pool composition, default correlation assumptions, and waterfall mechanics.

The role spans origination-side structuring and distribution-side positioning. You will work closely with Ornn's index and derivatives team to connect the structured products to our broader compute pricing infrastructure, and with engineering to ensure the platform can support the data and reporting requirements that rating agencies and investors demand.

What You'll Do

Design and iterate on the credit structures that transform diversified pools of non-IG compute tenant offtake into rated, investable instruments.

Build and maintain the quantitative models that drive pool composition, tranche sizing, credit enhancement levels, and stress testing across various default and correlation scenarios.

Own the rating agency relationship end to end: prepare materials, lead presentations, respond to methodology questions, and manage the ongoing surveillance process.

Define the waterfall mechanics, subordination levels, and reserve account structures for each product variant.

Work with the founders and legal counsel to structure the SPV and issuer-level documentation, ensuring alignment between the financial engineering and the legal architecture.

Develop the investor-facing materials, including offering memoranda, pool performance reports, and credit surveillance updates, that institutional buyers expect.

What We're Looking For

Requirements

 - 2+ years of experience in structured finance, securitization, or credit structuring at an investment bank, rating agency, specialty finance company, or structured credit fund.

 - Direct experience building or analyzing cash flow waterfalls, tranche structures, and credit enhancement mechanisms for pooled asset classes (ABS, CLOs, CMBS, or similar).

 - Demonstrated proficiency working with credit rating agencies on new issuance or surveillance, including preparing rating agency presentations and responding to methodology-driven diligence.

 - Strong quantitative modeling skills.

 - Familiarity with the credit characteristics of non-investment grade corporate obligors, including how to assess creditworthiness for companies with strong revenue growth but limited credit history.

 - Clear written and verbal communication.

Nice-to-Haves

Experience rating or analyzing the credit of technology companies, cloud infrastructure providers, or AI/ML companies specifically.

Background at a rating agency with direct exposure to new asset class methodology development.

Interest in or exposure to securitized debt markets, including ABS, whole business securitization, or esoteric asset classes.

Graduate degree from a top finance program (MBA, MFE, or equivalent).

Why This Role Is Important to Arcadia
Analytics sits at the center of how Arcadia turns complex healthcare data into better outcomes and smarter decisions.
On the product side, that means building and owning the productized analytics engines — risk, medical economics, episodes-of-care, and more — that power Arcadia's platform company-wide, built once and delivered at scale across our entire customer base.
On the Customer Insights side, that means going deep on a specific customer's specific problem: custom data models, bespoke dashboards, advisory work, and long-running embedded programs that don't fit a one-size-fits-all product. We describe Customer Insights' work as sitting between a platform and a plan — more customized and hands-on than an off-the-shelf reporting product, more flexible and embedded in the customer's actual decisions than a traditional outsourced consulting engagement.
We're currently hiring for several closely related analyst roles across this broader Analytics organization — spanning ownership of one of Arcadia's core analytics engines, program-specific analytical development for a major state Medicaid risk-stratification initiative,  a ground-up registry build for a national quality organization, versatile project and retainer delivery across our health system and payer customers, and dedicated analytics support for a major national health plan's Medicaid program. The skills and experience below are characteristic across these roles as a set — not every requirement applies to every specific seat, and we don't expect any one candidate to bring all of it. We'll work with you during the interview process to identify which role is the best fit for your background and interests.

Be a credible, independent presence in front of the customers or partners tied to your engagement

In this role, you will oversee revenue accounting operations, strengthen financial governance, and ensure accurate and reliable reporting across healthcare services. Your responsibilities will include:
- 
 Lead the monthly revenue close process in accordance with ASC 606, overseeing journal entries, accruals, reserves, and reconciliations to ensure accurate, audit-ready financial statements.
- 
 Oversee financial governance of outsourced Revenue Cycle Management (RCM) partners, monitoring service-level agreements (SLAs) and performance indicators such as claim denials, clean-claim rates, and net collection rates.
- 
 Hold external vendors accountable for performance targets, corrective actions, remediation plans, and operational improvements.
- 
 Identify and investigate revenue leakage, reimbursement shortfalls, unbilled services, missed authorizations, and other billing inefficiencies.
- 
 Collaborate with cross-functional teams to recover lost revenue, improve reimbursement outcomes, and strengthen cash conversion.
- 
 Reconcile completed patient visits, billable services, insurance claims, cash postings, and unapplied cash between RCM subledgers and NetSuite.
- 
 Manage accounts receivable valuation, aging schedules, collectability assessments, implicit price concessions, contractual allowances, and bad debt reserves across different payers and markets.
- 
 Validate claim-level financial data against reported financial statements, ensuring accurate payment posting, effective aged receivables management, and timely collections.
- 
 Establish and maintain internal controls, write-off approval processes, and segregation of duties across revenue operations.
- 
 Lead improvements to NetSuite and RCM system integrations, automating reconciliations, exception reporting, and financial controls while reducing manual processes.

 Partner with Operations, Finance, and Technology teams to develop automated dashboards and eliminate recurring operational bottlenecks.
- 
 Analyze revenue per visit, payer mix, and market trends to support budgeting, executive forecasting, and pricing decisions.

 The ideal candidate combines strong technical accounting expertise with specialized knowledge of healthcare reimbursement and revenue cycle operations. You should demonstrate:
- 
 Bachelor's degree in Accounting, Finance, or a related field.
- 
 7+ years of progressive accounting experience, with a strong foundation in revenue recognition under ASC 606, accounts receivable valuation, and internal controls.
- 
 In-depth knowledge of healthcare reimbursement models, insurance claims workflows, and Revenue Cycle Management (RCM).
- 
 Advanced Microsoft Excel skills and experience working with modern Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) systems.
- 
 Proven ability to analyze complex billing subledgers, reconcile large datasets, and identify financial discrepancies.
- 
 Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to translate complex financial information into actionable business insights.
- 
 Experience establishing financial controls, managing reconciliations, and improving revenue reporting processes.
- 
 Excellent communication and collaboration skills, with the ability to work effectively across Finance, Operations, Technology, and external vendor teams.
 Strongly Preferred Qualifications:

 Active Certified Public Accountant (CPA) license.

 Hands-on experience with NetSuite implementations, system integrations, or ERP optimization projects.
- 
 Previous experience in outpatient healthcare, physical therapy, or multi-site clinic operations.
- 
 Experience managing outsourced RCM vendors, including SLA monitoring, remediation plans, performance reviews, and vendor audits.
- 
 Familiarity with business intelligence and data analysis tools such as Power BI or SQL.

Coinspaid Solutions is a fintech company building blockchain payment infrastructure for the global economy.
We design, implement, and scale payment systems that connect digital assets with real-world financial operations. Our solutions help businesses and financial institutions operate efficiently in the evolving digital asset landscape.
For over 11 years, we’ve been developing products that bring crypto payments closer to mainstream adoption. Today, our team includes 350+ professionals working remotely across multiple countries.
We combine the pace of fintech with a long-term approach to building products, teams, and careers. As a remote-first company, we give people flexibility in how they work while maintaining strong collaboration and shared ownership across teams.
🏆 In 2026, Coinspaid was recognized as Best Corporate Culture in the Blockchain Industry in Europe, reflecting our focus on ownership, trust, and collaboration.
 


Coinspaid is building out Product Operations — the function that owns how our product is configured, deployed, and monitored in production, and ensures it performs correctly for clients and markets. Operations Manager works directly with the Head of Product Operations to take operational ownership of our highest-priority processes.
You'll be the person who makes sure product configuration, releases, and client setup are controlled, traceable, and never a surprise in production. This is a senior, hands-on individual contributor role for someone who wants to build the operating model for a function from the ground up, not maintain one that already exists.

What You'll Do
Own product configuration in production — active features, available assets and flows, operational parameters and limits — and keep it consistent, visible, and traceable at all times.
Coordinate deployments and releases — decide where and when capabilities are activated, confirm operational readiness before go-live, and bridge the gap between product delivery and real usage.

The ideal candidate is organized, fast, and relentless about follow-through. Prior fundraising experience is a plus but not required. ChowNow is one of the leading players in off-premise restaurant technology. As takeout becomes a vital revenue stream for independent restaurants, our platform helps owners focus on what they do best—serving great food—by offering solutions across the entire digital dining experience. From building branded websites and mobile apps, to powering online orders, managing menus, consolidating delivery, and running targeted marketing, we give restaurants the tools to grow on their own terms.
 
We support thousands of restaurants across North America, helping process $1B+ in gross food sales while saving our partners over $700M in third-party commission fees. Through our white-label ordering solutions, a growing demand network (including Google, Yelp, Apple, and Snap), and a diner-friendly marketplace, we empower independent restaurants to own their customer relationships and avoid inflated pricing and fees charged by 3rd party delivery apps like Uber and Doordash. 
 
Founded in 2012, we’ve navigated rapid growth and transformation—from startup roots through the pandemic boom—and are now beginning an exciting new era under our CEO, Kanika Soni. You put restaurants first. You deeply understand the importance of local restaurants and put them at the center of everything you do. You aim to help them not only survive but thrive.
 
You celebrate diversity. You recognize that diversity and inclusivity matter. •    Promote a strong risk culture through education, communication, collaboration, and constructive challenge.

 The Commercial Strategy & Revenue Operations team exists to solve some of TheGuarantors' highest-priority commercial challenges. We identify opportunities to grow the business, develop strategies to capture them, and work across the organization to turn those strategies into measurable results. 
 Our work spans every part of the commercial organization. We partner closely with Sales, Product, Risk, Marketing, Finance, and Operations to improve how we serve customers, launch new initiatives, strengthen our go-to-market strategy, and build the capabilities that enable the business to scale. Because our work cuts across functions, success depends on building trusted partnerships, influencing without formal authority, and aligning teams around a common goal. 
 We aren't an internal consulting team. We own initiatives from strategy through execution and are accountable for the impact they create. The people who thrive here are comfortable with ambiguity, motivated by ownership, and excited to solve difficult business problems. 
 The Opportunity 
 As a Commercial Strategy Associate focused on AM (Account Management) Strategy, you'll help shape how TheGuarantors grows its existing customer relationships and how our Account Management organization serves them. 
 Our customer base represents a significant source of future growth, but capturing that opportunity requires making thoughtful choices about where we invest, how we segment and serve different customers, and how we identify and pursue opportunities for deeper engagement. You'll develop the strategies and operating approaches that help our Account Managers focus on the highest-impact opportunities and turn strong customer relationships into sustained commercial growth. 
 This role is designed for someone who wants to move beyond analysis and become an operator. You'll work directly with Account Managers and AM leadership, analyze customer and portfolio performance, and own initiatives from strategy through execution. Over time, you'll also develop firsthand relationships with customers—joining important client discussions and business reviews to better understand their priorities and translate those insights into better commercial strategies. 
 Your success will ultimately be measured by whether the strategies and initiatives you help build make our Account Management organization more effective and create better outcomes for our customers and TheGuarantors. 
 This is a hybrid role based in NYC . 
 What You'll Do 
- Partner closely with Account Managers and AM leadership to identify challenges, evaluate opportunities, and implement high-impact improvements to drive customer growth, improve retention, and strengthen the effectiveness of our Account Management organization 
- Develop strategies that improve how we segment customers, allocate Account Management resources, and determine the right product offerings and engagement model for different parts of our portfolio 
- Translate insights from individual customers and customer segments into commercial strategies and initiatives that improve how we serve and grow our customer base 
- Help build customer-facing materials and strategic communications for our largest partnerships 
- Collaborate across Sales, Product, Risk, Pricing, Data, Marketing, and Operations to address customer needs, remove barriers to growth, and improve how we serve customers 
- Develop and improve the strategies, tools, and operating approaches that support effective customer planning, business reviews, executive engagement, and growth initiatives 
- Develop a firsthand understanding of customer priorities by joining client discussions and business reviews, and translate those insights into broader commercial strategies and improvements 
- Analyze customer and portfolio performance to identify trends, uncover opportunities for expansion or deeper engagement, and inform strategic decision-making 
 What You'll Bring 
- 2+ years
